8B.01.b:
### Point & say — the portals
| Portal | Where | At risk |
|---|---|---|
| **Anteromedial** (first) | Joint line, just **medial to TA** (tibialis anterior) | Saphenous nerve + vein → fewest structures (Netter; Campbell) |
| **Anterolateral** | Joint line, just **lateral to peroneus tertius**, under vision with a needle | **SPN** (intermediate dorsal cutaneous) |
| **Posterolateral** | Lateral edge of the Achilles, ≈1 cm above the fibular tip (Netter) | **Sural nerve** + small saphenous vein |
| Posteromedial (hindfoot endoscopy only) | Same level, medial to the Achilles, aimed at the scope | **Tibial bundle** → only with the scope already in, stay lateral to FHL (flexor hallucis longus) (Campbell) |
| Anterocentral | Between the extensors | DP (dorsalis pedis) artery + DPN (deep peroneal nerve) → avoid (Netter) |

[[FIG: Fig 8B.3, 8B.4, 8B.5, 8B.6, 8B.7 · 8B.01

- Position → supine, thigh holder, foot hanging → gravity distraction (Campbell)
- **Mark the SPN first** in plantar flexion + inversion → transillumination does not show it (Campbell)
- An SPN branch lies near the anterolateral portal in **68%** (Campbell)
- Nick the skin only, then spread with a hemostat (Voto 1989)

### Technique and hindfoot endoscopy
- Anterior tibial artery ≈2–3 mm from the anterior capsule → no blind shaver anteriorly (Campbell)
- Hindfoot endoscopy → **prone**, two portals beside the Achilles; **FHL = the medial border of safety** (Campbell)
- Commonest complication → **nerve injury**; suture the portals → no sinus (Campbell)
- Posteromedial portal → hemostat aimed at the **1st web space** until it touches bone, then stay lateral to FHL (Campbell)

- **Anterolateral** → lateral to peroneus tertius → **SPN**, marked in plantar flexion + inversion
- **Posterolateral** → beside the Achilles, 1 cm above the fibular tip → sural nerve
- Avoid anterocentral (DP artery, DPN) · nick the skin, spread, suture the portals

8B.02.b:
### Step by step
| Step | Anterior approach (Hopp) |
|---|---|
| Uses | Ankle **arthrodesis**, total ankle replacement, pilon ORIF, infection, loose bodies |
| Position | Supine, thigh tourniquet |
| Incision | **15 cm** longitudinal, from 10 cm above the joint, midway between the malleoli |
| Interval | **EHL / EDL** (extensor hallucis / digitorum longus) → both deep peroneal → **no true internervous plane** |
| Superficial | Skin only (SPN branches) → fascia + extensor retinaculum in line; find EHL–EDL a few cm above the joint |
| Deep | Bundle just medial to EHL → retract **EHL + bundle medially**, EDL laterally → longitudinal capsulotomy |
| Extension | Proximally between tibia and TA; distal extension rarely needed |

[[FIG: Fig 8B.8, 8B.9, 8B.10, 8B.11, 8B.12, 8B.13, 8B.14 · 8B.02

- **EHL crosses the bundle** from lateral to medial at the joint → bundle is TA–EHL above, EHL–EDL below (Hopp)
- Alternative **TA–EHL** interval → TA medial, bundle + toe extensors lateral (Campbell)
- Anterior approach reaches the **medial gutter**, which anterolateral and extensile approaches miss (Campbell)
- Repair the extensor retinacula → no bowstringing (Hopp)

| At risk | Why | Protect |
|---|---|---|
| **SPN** branches | Cross the ankle in the anterior midline | Skin-only cut; find and retract them |
| **Anterior tibial artery + DPN** | Under EHL; worst danger during the skin incision | **Partial exsanguination** → veins stay blue → bundle easy to find (Hopp); retract with EHL |
| TA tendon sheath | Opened → wound breakdown over the tendon | Keep the sheath closed (AO) |

8B.03.b:
### Choosing the approach (AO)
- **Large anterolateral fragment** with a medial plane near the malleolus → **anteromedial**; small, more lateral fragment → **anterolateral**
  [[FIG: Fig 8B.15, 8B.16 · 8B.03
- **Varus** pattern (medial comminution) → anteromedial buttress; **valgus** (lateral comminution) → anterolateral
- Open wound → plan the other side; incisions decided at the first debridement and ex-fix

### Staged protocol
1) **Span** → ex-fix (± fibula) → CT after the frame (Handbook; Campbell)
2) Wait for **skin wrinkles** → definitive ORIF at 10–21 days (Campbell)
3) Reduce **posterior → medial → central → anterolateral** (Campbell)
4) Fix → **articular K-wires → metaphysis → anteromedial plate**; distal screws before proximal (Handbook)

### Step by step
| Step | Anteromedial (AO) | Anterolateral (AO) |
|---|---|---|
| Incision | From 5–8 cm above the joint, **just lateral to the tibial crest** → toward the navicular | Centred at the joint, between tibia and fibula, along the **4th MT** (metatarsal); ≤7 cm above the joint |
| Interval | Medial to TA, sheath kept intact | Under the SPN → retinaculum → anterior compartment + peroneus tertius retracted medially |
| Reaches | Medial plafond + malleolus; medial plate | Chaput fragment, whole plafond to the medial malleolus; EDB (extensor digitorum brevis) off → talar neck |
| At risk | **Saphenous vein + nerve**, TA sheath, anterior fragment vessels | **SPN** (crosses the incision above the ankle) |

[[FIG: Fig 8B.17, 8B.18, 8B.19, 8B.20, 8B.21, 8B.22, 8B.23 · 8B.03

- **Assal extensile** → 0.5 cm lateral to TA, curving to the medial malleolus (Campbell)
- Keep its apex angle **>120°** → no apex necrosis (Campbell)
- **Posterolateral** → posterior fragment + fibula through one wound (AO) → 8B.06
- **Posteromedial** → posterior + medial fragments; windows behind TP (tibialis posterior), TP–FDL (flexor digitorum longus) or FDL–FHL (AO)

CLINICAL PEARL — pilon skin
- Skin bridge **≈7 cm**; straight incisions, never undermine (Campbell; AO)
- Ex-fix pins **away from future incisions**; no talar half-pin → calcaneal pin (Campbell)
- Old scar → go **through it**, never parallel to it (Campbell)
- Blood blisters → full-thickness damage → wait (Handbook)

8B.04.t: Medial Malleolus & Medial Side of the Ankle
8B.04.b:
### Step by step
| Step | Medial malleolus (Hopp) |
|---|---|
| Uses | Medial malleolar ORIF; transmalleolar access to the talar dome (osteotomy) |
| Position | Supine; the leg falls into natural external rotation |
| Incision | **10 cm curved**, centred just **anterior** to the tip, not over the bone (Hopp; AO) |
| Interval | None → straight onto subcutaneous bone |
| Superficial | Save the **great saphenous vein** → two saphenous nerve branches bound to it |
| Deep | Small **anterior capsulotomy** → see the joint, impaction (vertical fractures); split superficial deltoid for screw heads |
| Extension | Proximally along the subcutaneous tibia; distally to the deltoid and talonavicular joint |

[[FIG: Fig 8B.24, 8B.25, 8B.26, 8B.27, 8B.28, 8B.29, 8B.30, 8B.31, 8B.32 · 8B.04

- **Posterior incision** variant → retract TP anteriorly → sees posterior fragments but cannot fix them → lag from anterior (Hopp)
- Fix → **2 parallel cannulated screws**, anterior first (Handbook); strip as little as possible → fragments die if bare (Hopp)
- Saphenous nerve cut → painful neuroma + numb medial dorsum (Hopp)
- Lag technique → **near cortex at the outer diameter**, far cortex at the core diameter (Handbook)

### Medial malleolar osteotomy (talar body)
1) Pre-drill and tap for **two screws** before cutting (AO; Campbell)
[[FIG: Fig 8B.33, 8B.34, 8B.35, 8B.36, 8B.37 · 8B.04
2) Saw at the junction with the shaft, oblique, **stop at the subchondral bone**, finish with an osteotome (AO; Handbook)
3) Reflect the malleolus distally on the deltoid → **do not over-retract** (deltoid artery) (AO)
4) Protect the TP tendon behind and the talar dome with flat retractors (AO)

PITFALL — screws for the osteotomy
- Hopp → one screw + 2 K-wires (no interdigitation); Campbell and AO → **two lag screws**
- Say → "**two parallel lag screws perpendicular to the cut, pre-drilled before the osteotomy**"

8B.05.b:
### Step by step
| Step | Posteromedial (Hopp) |
|---|---|
| Uses | Clubfoot release, tarsal tunnel, posterior capsule, posteromedial fragment |
| Position | Supine with the ankle on the opposite knee, or lateral, operated leg down |
| Incision | **8–10 cm**, midway between the medial malleolus and the Achilles |
| Superficial | Fat between Achilles and flexors → incise flexor fascia **well away** from the malleolus |
| Deep | Route 1: **FHL / peronei**, FHL medially · Route 2: **bundle + FHL laterally / FDL medially** |
| Extension | Curve distally over the talonavicular joint → **master knot of Henry** |

[[FIG: Fig 8B.38, 8B.39, 8B.40, 8B.41, 8B.42, 8B.43, 8B.44 · 8B.05

- **FHL = the only muscle still fleshy** at this level → the landmark (Hopp)
- Child → tibial nerve surprisingly large, FDL tiny → identify before cutting (Hopp)
- Tarsal tunnel contents and order → 8A 8.11

| At risk | Why | Protect |
|---|---|---|
| **Posterior tibial artery + tibial nerve** | Between FDL and FHL ("Tom, Dick and Harry") | Find first; no forceful retraction (neurapraxia) |
| TP + FDL tendons | Right behind the malleolus | Keep their sheaths |
| Saphenous vein + nerve | Distal end | Retract anteriorly |

8B.06.b:
### Step by step
| Step | Posterolateral (Hopp; AO) |
|---|---|
| Uses | **Posterior malleolus (Volkmann)** + fibula through one incision; posterior pilon; posterior subtalar fusion |
| Position | **Prone** (or lateral) |
| Incision | **10 cm**, midway between the fibula and the lateral Achilles, up from the fibular tip |
| Interval | **Peroneus brevis (SPN) / FHL (tibial)** → true internervous plane |
| Superficial | Sural nerve + small saphenous vein anterior to the incision → keep as one unit |
| Deep | Peronei laterally → lift lateral FHL fibres off the fibula → FHL medially → posterior tibia |
| Extension | Between lateral gastrocnemius and peronei to the posterolateral tibia |

- Fibula through the same skin → retract peronei the other way → posterior plate (AO)
- **Do not dissect between the posterior malleolus and fibula** → keeps the posterior inferior tibiofibular ligament (Campbell)
- Screws for the posterior malleolus → **posterior → anterior** (Handbook)
- Posterior antiglide plate is strongest but irritates the peronei (Handbook)

EXAM PEARL — prone or not?
- Plus → fixes the **Volkmann fragment and fibula together** under direct vision (Handbook; AO)
- Minus → prone makes the medial side awkward (Hopp)
- Answer → posterolateral prone first, then turn supine for the medial malleolus (Handbook)

| At risk | Why | Protect |
|---|---|---|
| **Sural nerve** | Parallel to the lateral Achilles margin | Stay in the midline between fibula and Achilles |
| Peroneal artery / vein | Deep, near the posterior tibia | Deflate the tourniquet before closure (AO) |
| Peroneal tendons | Retracted, may sublux | Repair the retinaculum |

### Step by step
| Step | Lateral malleolus (Hopp; AO) |
|---|---|
| Uses | Fibular ORIF; Chaput lesion and anterior syndesmosis (incision slightly anterior) |
| Position | Supine, sandbag under the buttock |
| Incision | **10–15 cm** along the fibula to the tip + 2 cm, curving slightly forward |
| Interval | None distally (subcutaneous bone); higher up **peroneus tertius (DPN) / peronei (SPN)** |
| Deep | **Strictly subperiosteal**; strip only the fracture site |
| Extension | Proximal → peronei / flexors plane; distal → calcaneocuboid joint |

[[FIG: Fig 8B.57, 8B.58, 8B.59, 8B.60 · 8B.07

- Don't fully divide the superior peroneal retinaculum → tendon subluxation (Campbell)
- Deflate the tourniquet before closure → peroneal artery branches bleed (Hopp)

- High fibula (Weber C) → same line centred on the fracture; protect the SPN (AO) (→ 8A 8.06)
- **TightRope** → stronger than a screw and needs no removal; the syndesmotic screw is removed (Handbook)

| At risk | Why | Protect |
|---|---|---|
| **SPN** | Anterior, crosses obliquely 3–18 cm up | Identify proximally; not in the closure |
| **Sural nerve** + small saphenous vein | Behind the fibula | Stay on the fibula |
| Peroneal artery terminal branches | Deep to the medial fibula | Haemostasis, drain |

### Extensile lateral vs sinus tarsi
| | **Extended lateral (L-shaped)** | **Sinus tarsi** |
|---|---|---|
| Use | All fracture types; Sanders IV plate (Handbook) | Displaced intra-articular, Sanders II–III (Handbook); within 10–14 days (Campbell) |
| Position | Lateral, operated leg up | Lateral |
| Incision | Vertical limb **at the lateral Achilles border** → horizontal limb at the sole-skin junction → **5th MT base** (AO) | **Fibular tip → 4th MT base**, over the posterior facet (AO; Campbell) |
| Flap | Full-thickness, **subperiosteal**, carries peronei + sural nerve; held by K-wires; no forceps (Campbell) | Peronei inferior, EDB partly reflected → subtalar joint |
| Sees | Whole lateral wall + posterior facet | Posterior facet + anterior calcaneus; tuberosity reduced indirectly |
| Problem | **Wound breakdown** at the apex | Less exposure of the tuberosity; **peroneal subluxation** common → settles after reduction (AO) |

- Close from both ends **toward the apex**; Allgöwer–Donati sutures; no vacuum dressing on the flap (Campbell)

8B.11.t: Forefoot — 1st MTP, Lesser MTPs, Web Spaces
8B.11.b:
### 1st MTP joint
| Step | Dorsomedial / medial (Hopp; Campbell) |
|---|---|
| Uses | Bunion procedures, distal osteotomy, Keller, arthrodesis, replacement, cheilectomy |
| Position | Supine; thigh tourniquet or ankle Esmarch |
| Incision | **Straight, just medial to EHL** (Campbell preferred) or curved dorsomedial over the joint (Hopp) |
| Interval | None → EHL and abductor hallucis supplied far proximally |
| Deep | Capsule flap based on the proximal phalanx (U or racquet) |

[[FIG: Fig 8B.93, 8B.94, 8B.95, 8B.96, 8B.97, 8B.98, 8B.99 · 8B.11

- Toe framed by the **dorsomedial cutaneous nerve** medially and the **DPN** laterally → protect both (Hopp; AO)
- **FHL** lies in a groove under the proximal phalanx → at risk during plantar stripping (Hopp)
- Full stripping before a distal osteotomy → **head avascular necrosis** (Hopp)
- Adductor hallucis = main deforming force in hallux valgus; abductor hallucis the only corrector (Hopp)

### Lesser MTPs and web spaces
- Lesser MTP (metatarsophalangeal) → 2–3 cm **dorsolateral** incision beside the long extensor; two joints → one incision between them (Hopp)
  [[FIG: Fig 8B.100, 8B.101, 8B.102, 8B.103, 8B.104, 8B.105, 8B.106, 8B.107, 8B.108 · 8B.11
- Plantar nerves and vessels lie **under the deep transverse MT ligament** → stay dorsal (Hopp)
- **Morton neuroma** → dorsal longitudinal web incision, 2–3 cm; open the deep transverse MT ligament; plantar pressure delivers the neuroma (Hopp)

### Toe and 5th MT safety
- Never operate on **both webs of one toe** at once → both digital arteries cut → toe ischaemia (Hopp)
- 5th MT → lateral incision at the junction of dorsal and plantar skin; **sural nerve branches** + small saphenous vein (AO)

8B.13.b:
### The three incisions
| Release | Incision | Note |
|---|---|---|
| **Turco** | Single **posteromedial**: 1st MT base → under the medial malleolus → medial to the Achilles (Handbook) | Poor plantar / posterolateral access; crosses medial creases; bundle at risk (Handbook) |
| **Carroll** | Medial (1st MT base curving to the heel) + **separate posterolateral** (Dr Fathey) | Adds plantar fascia release and CC capsulotomy; best exposure, fewer scar problems |
| **Cincinnati** | One **circumferential** cut: naviculocuneiform joint → under the medial malleolus → across the Achilles → past the sinus tarsi (Campbell) | Tight in dorsiflexion → cast in plantar flexion first, correct at 2 weeks (Campbell) |

[[FIG: Fig 8B.112 · 8B.13

- Timing → after 1 year or foot >8–9 cm; surgery "à la carte" → only what the foot needs (Dr Fathey)
- Dr Fathey adds a lateral incision to Turco when the lateral side is tight

### Release order (Dr Fathey)
1) **Abductor hallucis** → work above it, away from the bundle
2) **Plantar fascia** (+ flexor digitorum brevis, abductor digiti minimi in one cut if needed)
3) **TN joint** dorsal, plantar, medial · **CC** medial capsule only · medial subtalar
4) **Spring + deltoid** medially, **calcaneofibular ligament** laterally (cut near the calcaneus)
5) **TP** Z-lengthening ≥2.5 cm above the malleolus (Campbell) · Achilles Z-lengthening, distal cut medial
6) K-wires talus → navicular, then CC, before the posterior release

- **Never cut the interosseous talocalcaneal ligament** → lateral calcaneal shift → valgus (Dr Fathey; Campbell)
- Release the peroneal sheath, not the tendons; **don't disturb the dorsal talar vessels** (Dr Fathey; Campbell)
- Enough medial release → the navicular sits easily on the talar head (Dr Fathey)
- Talus should roll back ≥1.5 cm of cartilage; if not → posterior talofibular ligament, then posterior deep deltoid (Campbell)
